instruction: Make a service start only after PostgreSQL is up.
Use Wants for a soft dependency on a cache.
Order a worker after the broker but allow it to start if the broker fails.
Define a hard failure propagation using BindsTo.
Stop a dependent service when another one stops using PartOf.
Use Before to make a service finish before another starts.
Order a network service after network-online.target.
Add a requirement on a mount unit.
Use Conflicts to prevent two services running at once.
Order a service after a socket unit it uses.

Set up ordering so a cleanup runs after the main service stops.
output:
[Unit]
Description=Cleanup
After=app.service
PartOf=app.service

[Service]
Type=oneshot
RemainAfterExit=yes
ExecStop=/usr/local/bin/cleanup

instruction: Depend on a timer's service and order them correctly.
Avoid a common ordering pitfall: describe why After alone is insufficient.
output:
[Unit]
Description=Db client
# After= only orders; it does NOT pull in the dependency.
# Use Requires= or Wants= to actually start the other unit.
After=postgresql.service
Requires=postgresql.service

[Service]
ExecStart=/usr/local/bin/db-client

instruction: Set a job timeout for a slow dependency startup.
output:

Description=Slow starter
After=db.service
Requires=db.service
JobTimeoutSec=300

[Service]
ExecStart=/usr/local/bin/slow-starter
